concept.name: Size factor
concept.definition: A Fama-French stock factor measuring the return difference between small-capitalization and large-capitalization stocks: SMB (Small Minus Big) is the average return on the small-stock portfolios minus the average return on the big-stock portfolios formed on market equity.
concept.intuition: It isolates the historical tendency of small companies' stocks to behave differently - and on average to earn more - than big companies' stocks.
concept.mechanics: Stocks are sorted on market equity using NYSE breakpoints; SMB is the average return of the three small portfolios minus the average return of the three big portfolios from the 2x3 size-by-book-to-market sorts (in the five-factor model, averaged across the book-to-market, profitability, and investment sorts).
concept.formula: SMB = (1/3)(Small Value + Small Neutral + Small Growth) - (1/3)(Big Value + Big Neutral + Big Growth).
concept.failure_modes: The small-cap premium is episodic and much weaker after its publication in the early 1980s; SMB returns are also sensitive to breakpoint choices, microstructure noise in small caps, and whether January effects are included.
concept.misconceptions: SMB is not a bet that small stocks always beat big stocks - it is a long-short factor return that is negative in many periods, and loading on it measures exposure to whatever common shocks drive the small-big return gap.
concept.example: In a month when the three small-cap portfolios average 2.1% and the three big-cap portfolios average 0.6%, the SMB realization is +1.5%.

citations.source: Kenneth R. French Data Library, Description of Fama/French Factors
